findings.finding: The Q3 balance sheet will for the first time carry the July rights-issue proceeds and the SEK 57m Fenja loan, putting cash near SEK 280-300m against a market cap of about SEK 365m (282m shares x SEK 1.30), i.e. the stock trades at roughly 1.2-1.3x gross cash; the figure is derivable from the H1 report but has not yet been printed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cash/financing lines have been sold rather than bought here: the rights-issue outcome day (2026-06-24) -5.4%, and report days since Feb 2025 moved -1.8, -5.8, -3.6, -7.4, -11.5, -1.2, +2.6 (Yahoo tape).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the H1 report itself says its SEK 222m excludes the July proceeds and the loan, and management has stated runway to mid-2028, so anyone doing the arithmetic has it. What is not yet seen is the printed number and the issue costs; if the market had fully credited a ~SEK 290m cash pile the stock would not be at its 52-week low 40% below the rights-issue price, but a Swedish small-biotech discount to cash is common and this is a weak argument.
findings.independence: Runway-to-mid-2028 statement in the Q2 call summary, https://quartr.com/events/cantargia-canta-stifel-2026-healthcare-conference-2026_3sKX6je4

findings.finding: Cantargia's own report days have been sold: of the seven interim/year-end releases since Feb 2025 (dates from the MFN calendar) five closed down, with a mean of about -4% (-1.8, -5.8, -3.6, -7.4, -11.5, -1.2, +2.6), as a cash-burning biotech whose news flow runs through separate releases rather than the report.
findings.why_not_priced: A base rate rather than a fact about this print, and the larger down-days (Nov 2025, Feb 2026) carried trial or financing news this report is not expected to carry; the stock has already fallen 26% since 4 November, so some of the habitual selling may have happened. Sized small for that reason.
